card.title: Board: a ticket opens as a centered card modal (Trello-style) with click-to-edit, replacing the side panel
card.description:
Clicking a ticket opens a side panel (`.panel` in src/airlie/serve/web/app.css, built as `panel` in src/airlie/serve/web/screens/board.js) at a fixed 380px, which is too narrow to read. Open it instead as a centered modal over the board, the way Trello opens a card: focused and simple, not Jira's dense issue view.

Scope
- Mockups first: the design/ux roles mock up the card modal at desktop and 375px, and Noah approves them before anything is built.
- The board stays where it is behind a dimmed backdrop; the columns no longer give up width to a panel.
- Layout: a large title at the top with "in <status>" under it. The main column holds the description, then children, then comments. A narrow right column holds the actions: Move and Add child.
- The card is wide (about 768px, max-width bound) and scrolls with the page rather than having its own inner scrollbar.
- Close with X, Escape (when nothing is being edited) or a click on the backdrop. Focus stays inside the modal while it is open and goes back to the ticket that opened it.
- The URL stays #/board/AIR-n, so a reload or a link opens the modal over the board.
- The "New story/epic" form uses the same modal.
- Below 1024px the modal fills the screen, as the panel does now.
- Click-to-edit everywhere: every text section shows as text, and clicking it turns that spot into an editor. The separate "Edit" form goes away.
  - Title: click to get an input; Enter or clicking away saves, Escape cancels.
  - Description: click the rendered text to edit it in place; Save and Cancel buttons. Clicking a link inside it follows the link instead of editing. An empty description shows a clickable "Add a more detailed description…".
  - Repository and labels: click either to edit in place; an empty one shows a clickable prompt ("Add a repository").
  - Comments: click one of your own comments (written by the signed-in user) to edit it in place. Other authors' comments, airlie's roles included, stay read-only. The "Add a comment" box is always ready to type in.
- Rich editor: the description, comment and new-comment boxes are a Trello-style rich editor that renders markdown as you type (`**bold**` turns bold, `- ` starts a list, fenced code becomes a code block) with a small toolbar (bold, italic, list, link, code). Text is still stored as markdown, so the board API and airlie's agents see no change. The web app has no build step, so load a pinned editor library (TipTap or Milkdown, exact version) from a CDN or vendor a copy in the repo. It must round-trip everything AIR-18 renders: headings, bold, italic, lists, links, inline code, fenced code blocks, block quotes and tables.
- Pasting HTML into the editor stores markdown, never raw HTML, and nothing pasted can run script (AIR-18's safety rules hold).
- Clickable sections look clickable (hover background, text cursor), are reachable by Tab and open with Enter.
- One section is open for editing at a time; opening another saves the first. Escape inside an editor cancels that edit only.
- Editing comments is new server work: a PATCH /v1/board/items/{key}/comments/{id} endpoint that only the comment's author may use.
- Remove the side panel code and the resize work this story started earlier (layer 01 of the previous run).
- Build after AIR-18; reuse its markdown renderer (src/airlie/serve/web/md.js) for read-only text.

Done when
- Noah has approved the mockups.
- Clicking a ticket opens the modal over the dimmed board; X, Escape and a backdrop click each close it and return focus to that ticket.
- Reloading #/board/AIR-17 shows the modal.
- Clicking the title, description, repository, labels or one of your own comments opens it for editing in place; a save survives a reload and Escape discards the edit.
- Clicking a link in a description follows the link instead of opening an editor.
- Typing bold text, a list and a fenced code block into a comment shows them formatted before saving, and the saved comment renders the same after a reload; the stored text is markdown.
- Editing another author's comment is refused by the API, covered by a test.
- A long description reads comfortably without sideways scrolling.
- Checked in the running web app (task serve) at desktop and 375px.
- task check passes.

story.title: Board: open a ticket as a centered card modal with click-to-edit
story.summary: A person reading a board ticket needs the detail view to be a wide, centered, Trello-style card modal over the dimmed board instead of the current 380px side panel, with every text section editable in place and a new comment-edit endpoint. Why: the fixed 380px panel is too narrow to read a description, and the separate Edit form is a second, dense path to the same data; the modal makes the ticket focused and simple and lets a reader change a field without leaving the card.

acceptance.given: I am signed in on the board at desktop width (>=1024px) and the board columns are visible
acceptance.then: a card modal opens centered over the board behind a dimmed backdrop, the columns keep their full width (no panel column is reserved), and the modal shows a large title with the text "in <status>" directly under it

acceptance.then: the modal closes, the board is undimmed, focus returns to the ticket card that opened it, and the URL hash returns to #/board

out_of_scope: The Trello-style rich markdown editor (TipTap/Milkdown from a pinned CDN or vendored) with a bold/italic/list/link/code toolbar that renders markdown live as you type; this slice keeps the existing plain textarea for description, comment and new-comment boxes and the existing md.js for read-only rendering
Pasting HTML into an editor storing markdown / guaranteeing no pasted script runs (AIR-18 safety rules); deferred until the rich editor lands
Mockup approval by design/ux roles at desktop and 375px before build (a process gate, not a code deliverable)
The narrow right column holding the Move and Add child actions as a distinct layout; this slice keeps the existing status Move buttons and Add child button in the main column
Any change to the board API's item routes beyond adding the single comment-edit endpoint
Children list rendering changes beyond what the panel already showed
assumptions: The existing board API already returns item.description, item.labels, item.comments (each with an id, author, text, at), item.status, item.level, item.parent, created_at and created_by, and PATCH /v1/board/items/{key} accepts {title, description, labels}; only the comment-edit endpoint is new server work
The signed-in user's identity is available to the board screen (ctx) and matches the comment.author field, so the client can tell which comments are the user's own
The comment-edit endpoint is PATCH /v1/board/items/{key}/comments/{id} with a {text} body, returns the updated item, and is the only new route added
The existing md.js markdown() renderer is reused for all read-only text (description, comments) and the existing request() helper is used for all API calls
The URL scheme #/board/{key} is unchanged, so a reload or shared link opens the modal over the board
The story builds after AIR-18 (the markdown renderer) and reuses its md.js; no new markdown dependency is introduced in this slice

survey:
# Survey notes: Board card modal (replaces side panel)

## 1. Files and symbols the change touches

**Web (no build step; static files served from `src/airlie/serve/web/`)**
- `src/airlie/serve/web/screens/board.js` — all panel machinery lives here: `panel` (line 65, `aside.panel` inside `.board-body` at line 89), `closePanel` (217, navigates to `#/board` at 220), `panelFrame` (223), `openItem` (233: move buttons 268, description 269, the `<details>` "Edit" form 270–290, children 291–298, comments 299–325), `openNew` (331, also uses `panelFrame`). Card click → `ctx.go` (163); reload hook `if (key) openItem(key)` (105); cleanup only sets `gone` (371–373) — the modal must add/remove a document keydown listener and restore focus in cleanup.
- `src/airlie/serve/web/app.css` — `.panel` fixed 380px sticky (1160–1174), `.board-body` flex row (1094–1098), the `<1024px` full-screen panel media query (1199–1216) = the "resize work" to remove, global `[hidden]` (1070). Note the page scroll container is `.main` (333–338): "scrolls with the page, no inner scrollbar" means the card must scroll inside `.main`, which constrains the overlay CSS.
- `src/airlie/serve/web/app.js` — route `#/board/(key)` (line 13), `render(main, params, ctx)` + cleanup contract (130–165), `ctx.go` (105).
- `src/airlie/serve/web/md.js` — `markdown()` (imported board.js:5). I did **not** read it; planner must verify it renders tables and sanitizes (AIR-18's safety rules) since the round-trip criterion includes tables.
- `src/airlie/serve/web/api.js` — `whoami()` (used app.js:123). board.js currently doesn't know the signed-in user; it needs the username to mark own comments editable. Check `whoami`'s return shape.
- `src/airlie/serve/web/index.html` (643 B) — the one place to add a pinned CDN `<script>` (TipTap/Milkdown, exact version) if not vendoring.
- `src/airlie/serve/web/cards.js` — unread; board.js builds cards inline, so verify what it's for before touching.

**Server**
- `src/airlie/board/api.py` — `PERSON = "noah"` (line 16); `AddComment` (43); `add_comment` (108) → `store.comment(key, PERSON, body.text)`. New `PATCH /items/{key}/comments/{id}` goes inside `board_router` (48); router is included at `src/airlie/serve/app.py:210`, so no new registration. Docstring (1–3) says "a later per-person auth sets the author" — the endpoint must read the **actual signed-in user** from the request, not the constant; find how other `/v1` routes get identity (`src/airlie/auth/`, key middleware).
- `src/airlie/board/store.py` + `model.py` — unread. The endpoint needs a comment **id** and an update method. board.js only uses `c.author`/`c.at`/`c.text` (line 303); if comments have no stable id in the schema, the store must add one. Also check `jira_import.py`: imported comments may carry non-noah authors (the read-only case).

## 2. Where tests live / naming

- I did not list `tests/`. Map shows `tests/unit` (141), `tests/integration` (4), `tests/e2e` (6), `tests/live` (6), `tests/fixtures` (20). Planner must grep for existing board API tests and any web tests.
- `scripts/run_layer.py` (`has_tests(layer_dir)`) + `.github/workflows/mutation-weekly.yml` imply per-story "layer" test dirs; the request references "layer 01 of the previous run" — locate that directory and remove/replace its panel-resize tests.
- `scripts/web_e2e.py` (14.4 KB) is the likely harness for the "checked in the running web app (task serve) at desktop and 375px" criteria — read it for how browser tests are written/named.
- `Taskfile.yml` defines `task check` — read it to know the gate.

## 3. Conventions / registries a new name must join

- No config schema or tool list: the board API is a FastAPI router (`app.py:210`) and the web app is static — new names are just a route in `board_router` and CSS classes in `app.css`.
- Rich editor: no build step, so pinned CDN tag in `index.html` **or** vendored copy under `src/airlie/serve/web/`; pin the exact version. TipTap needs the Table extension for the round-trip criterion; Milkdown's default preset may not do tables — verify before choosing.
- Mockups: request requires design/ux mockups + Noah approval before build; check `docs/` (83 files) / `knowledge/` for where prior mockups were stored.

## 4. Things that could make a test pass for the wrong reason

- **Author check**: with `PERSON="noah"` and all v1 comments authored by noah, a "another author's comment refused" test must create a comment with a *different* author via the store (`store.comment(key, "airlie", …)`), and the endpoint must compare against the request's signed-in user, not the constant — otherwise the test passes while multi-user is broken.
- **Comment rendering**: board.js:303 renders `c.text` as a plain text node; the "saved comment renders the same after a reload" criterion requires `markdown()` output. Pin the expected HTML; a text-node assertion passes today and fails after the change.
- **Panel removal**: a "no side panel" test must assert absence of `.panel` *and* that `.columns` keeps full width with the modal open. A hidden-but-present panel, or a modal inserted into `.board-body`'s flex (app.css:1094), would silently shrink the columns again.
- **Escape**: two behaviors (close modal vs cancel active editor). A test asserting only "Escape closes" passes even if editor-cancel is broken; test both, with an editor focused.
- **Focus return**: `drawColumns()` clears and rebuilds cards (board.js:197–214), so the original card element is gone after any re-render; close must re-find the card by `dataset.key` (171). A test that closes without a re-render in between passes with a stale-element focus.
- **Link vs edit**: the description click handler must let `<a>` clicks through; the test must assert navigation / default-not-prevented, not just "no editor opened" (a handler swallowing all clicks passes the weaker assertion).
- **Close and hash**: current `closePanel` navigates to `#/board` (board.js:220); the request says the URL stays `#/board/AIR-n`. Decide in the mockup whether close keeps the hash (reload reopens via the line-105 hook) or clears it.
- **<1024px full-screen**: the old `.panel` media query (app.css:1199–1216) must be *removed*, not just overridden — a computed-style check at 375px passes with the old rule still present if the new rule wins by specificity.
- **"New story/epic" form**: `openNew` (331) uses `panelFrame` and must move to the same modal; after create it `ctx.go`s to the new key (353), which will open the item modal — make sure that path is covered, not just the button.

layers.title: Give board comments a stable id and an edit method
layers.scope: src/airlie/board/model.py, src/airlie/board/store.py, every other Comment( construction found by grep (e.g. src/airlie/board/jira_import.py), and the existing board store tests in tests/ (locate by grepping for BoardStore)
layers.brief: Foundation only, no API or UI. (1) Add `id: int` as the first field of the frozen Comment dataclass in model.py — the SQLite comments table already has `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`; Item.to_dict() uses asdict, so the id reaches JSON automatically. (2) In BoardStore._item(), select `id` in the comments query and construct Comment(c['id'], c['author'], c['text'], c['at']). (3) Add BoardStore.edit_comment(key: str, comment_id: int, text: str) -> Item: under the lock, one transaction — self._get(key) (KeyError for an unknown item), UPDATE comments SET text = ? WHERE item_key = ? AND id = ?, raise KeyError when rowcount is 0, bump the item's updated_at, return self._get(key). (4) Grep the repo for other positional Comment( constructions (jira_import.py is the likely one) and update them to pass the id. Tests (extend the existing board store test file, found by grepping tests/ for BoardStore): edit_comment changes the stored text and bumps updated_at; it raises KeyError for a comment id that exists on another item and for an unknown item; to_dict() of an item with a comment includes the comment id. All fail before (no id field, no method) and pass after.

layers.title: PATCH /v1/board/items/{key}/comments/{id} with an author check
layers.scope: src/airlie/board/api.py and the existing board API tests in tests/ (locate by grepping for board_router or /v1/board); no change to serve/app.py (the router is already included at app.py:210) and no change to the existing item routes
layers.brief: Add one route inside board_router: class EditComment(BaseModel) with model_config extra='forbid' and text: str, and @router.patch('/items/{key}/comments/{comment_id}') async def edit_comment(key: str, comment_id: int, body: EditComment, request: Request). The endpoint must read the actual signed-in user, never the PERSON constant: principal = getattr(request.state, 'principal', None); if it is None raise HTTPException(401, 'not signed in') (the serve middleware sets it for every /v1 route, but a bare-router test must not 500). Then item(key) for the 404; find the comment in the item's comments where c['id'] == comment_id, else HTTPException(404, f'no comment {comment_id} on {key}'); if comment['author'] is neither principal.name nor principal.user_id raise HTTPException(403, 'you can only edit your own comments') — the body must contain the exact phrase 'can only edit your own comments' (AC16). Otherwise return store.edit_comment(key, comment_id, body.text).to_dict(). Tests must run through create_app(..., api_key=...) so the principal middleware runs (with the api-key principal, name and user_id are both 'api-key'): (a) happy path — create the comment via the store with an author equal to the test principal's name/user_id, PATCH it, assert 200 and the returned item's comment text is the new text; (b) the 403 — create a comment via the store with a different author (e.g. 'airlie') and assert status 403 and the phrase in the body; never rely on PERSON matching the principal, since with all-noah comments the wrong-reason version would pass; (c) unknown comment id returns 404. The existing board API tests must keep passing unchanged.

layers.title: Replace the 380px side panel with a centered card modal
layers.scope: src/airlie/serve/web/screens/board.js, src/airlie/serve/web/app.css, and the web e2e tests (follow the existing pattern in scripts/web_e2e.py / tests/e2e/)
layers.brief: In board.js: delete the panel aside (line 65), closePanel and panelFrame; add a modal element (a backdrop div plus a card div, role='dialog', aria-modal='true', labelled by the title) appended as a sibling of .board-body inside the board page — never inside .board-body's flex, so the columns keep full width (AC1). openItem renders into the card: a large title (h2) with the text 'in <status>' directly under it (AC1), the existing status chips, Move buttons, Add child, children list and comments section (still plain for now), and the created/updated footer. openNew (New initiative, and Add child's New story/epic) renders its form into the same card (AC20). Close paths: the X button, a click on the backdrop (not the card), and Escape while no editor is open — each removes the modal, undims the board, restores focus to the card that opened it re-found by dataset.key (drawColumns rebuilds cards, so never keep the stale element), and ctx.go('#/board') (AC2). The reload hook `if (key) openItem(key)` in load() is unchanged, so #/board/AIR-17 reopens the modal (AC3). While the modal is open, install a document keydown listener (Escape) and a Tab focus trap that cycles focus among the card's focusable elements so focus never reaches the board behind the backdrop (AC21); the screen's cleanup function must remove both listeners and the modal (today it only sets gone). In app.css: delete the .panel rules (380px sticky, the .board-body flex child, the <1024px full-screen panel media query) and any resize/width-resize handler for the detail view (AC22); add the card rules — desktop: centered, max-width 768px, overflow visible so it scrolls with the .main page container and text wraps (no horizontal scrollbar, no inner scrollbar, AC18); a <1024px media query making backdrop and card position fixed inset 0 (AC19). Browser tests (follow the repo's existing web e2e pattern): with the modal open assert there is no element with class 'panel', the columns keep full width and the backdrop is dimmed (AC1/AC22 — the absence is proven inside the test that opens the modal); Escape with no editor closes it, undims, returns focus to the card and sets the hash to #/board (AC2); reload at #/board/AIR-17 reopens the modal with the same title and 'in <status>' line (AC3); at desktop width the card is at most 768px wide with no horizontal overflow and no inner scrollbar (AC18); at 375px the card is fixed inset 0 (AC19); the New initiative form opens in the same centered modal (AC20); repeated Tab stays inside the modal (AC21).

layers.title: In-place editing of every text section, including own comments
layers.scope: src/airlie/serve/web/screens/board.js (and app.css only for editor styling), plus the web e2e tests
layers.brief: Add one shared section-editor mechanism to the card: clicking a section hides its rendered text and shows an editor pre-filled with the current value plus Save and Cancel; Save issues the PATCH, Cancel and Escape discard; Enter or clicking away (blur) saves; opening any section first saves any other open one, so at most one section is ever open (AC13). Apply it to: the title (input; AC12); the description — rendered via markdown() when non-empty (AC4: click turns it into a textarea pre-filled with the current description, rendered text hidden while editing), an empty description shows the clickable prompt 'Add a more detailed description…' that opens an empty editor (AC8), and a click on a rendered <a> must not open the editor and must not be prevented so the link opens in a new tab (AC7); the repository — empty shows the clickable 'Add a repository' prompt, set shows the owner/name text; both become an input, and saving rewrites the repo:<owner>/<name> label via the existing labelsFrom/REPO helpers and PATCH /v1/board/items/{key} (AC9/AC10); the other labels — comma-separated input pre-filled with the non-repo labels, saving updates labels (AC11). Description and label saves go through the existing patch() to PATCH /v1/board/items/{key} with {title, description, labels} and re-render the card from the returned item, so the updated markdown shows and survives a reload (AC5). Comments: render each comment's text via markdown() (not a plain text node), and fetch whoami() once on board load; a comment is editable (click opens a pre-filled editor, Save PATCHes /v1/board/items/{key}/comments/{id} with {text} using the comment id from layer 1) only when c.author matches the whoami name or user_id — otherwise it stays read-only with no editor affordance (AC14/AC15). The Escape document listener from the modal layer now branches: an open editor is cancelled (rendered text reverts, modal stays open with other sections intact — AC6/AC17) and only with no editor open does Escape close the modal. Browser tests must cover both Escape branches with an editor focused so neither passes by accident; the 403 from the API layer surfaces as the existing error line, not a silent revert.
